solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Less than half fluent radio broadcast taken by Trump

definitions.note: a participial phrase standing for the noun: a state Trump won

indicators.note: keeping fewer than half of a six-letter word means only its opening couple of letters survive
broadcasting scatters things widely, so the word before it is scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the first two of six letters, which is less than half
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking radio campaign helps Trump win over a few listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Florida is the state Trump carried in his elections and where his Mar-a-Lago home sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunshine State voted Republican in Trump's presidential races, so it was a prize he won.

clue.text: Alternative facts – great theatrical stuff

indicators.note: an alternative version of something is a different arrangement of it, so the following words are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at Trump's team and their 'alternative facts', praised as great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative facts' was the phrase Kellyanne Conway used in 2017 to defend false White House claims, so the surface reads as a political jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in putting on plays, scenery and effects is the craft of the stage, broadly theatrical matters.

clue.text: Showing poor taste, Gordon allied with Tony finally?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the name just before it

blocks.note: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero
the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown teaming up with Tony Blair, presented as a lapse of political taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the two Labour leaders, Gordon Brown and Tony Blair, but Gordon is the science-fiction hero Flash Gordon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gaudy and ostentatious, designed to impress, is vulgar and lacks refinement.

clue.text: Refrain is "Endless burden, that's what Trump represents"

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a chore is a tiresome task, a burden
as president Trump represents the United States

explanation.surface: A complaint that Trump is a never-ending burden, phrased like a protest chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning hold back, but it is the noun for the repeated part of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated section sung after each verse of a song is its recurring line, the bit everyone joins in.

clue.text: Make out with smooth, high-up intelligence gatherer

blocks.note: to make out something distant is to spot it
to plane wood is to make it smooth

explanation.surface: A racy suggestion of kissing someone smooth, then a sudden turn to espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' suggests snogging, but here it means to discern or see.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance aircraft flies at great altitude to photograph and monitor enemy territory for military information.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Reliable voting indicator, once one disheartened Donald – crazy, LOL!

indicators.note: losing its heart, the surname keeps only its outer letters with the middle cut out
crazy means jumbled and disordered, so the letters after it are mixed up

blocks.note: ex means former, once
the Roman numeral for one
Donald Trump's surname
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeer that exit polls once held up, until Trump's 2016 surprise left them laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP without its middle RUM leaves TP. The surface's 'once' is a dig: the polls that once seemed reliable were wrong about Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveys of people leaving polling stations are used to forecast an election result before counting finishes.

clue.text: Female sporting Lycra – no!

definitions.note: a female name, not the adjective

indicators.note: sporting can mean playful, frolicking, so the letters play about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of Lycra plus no, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman wearing Lycra and someone crying out against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like it means wearing, which fits the Lycra, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolyn is a woman's given name, so it stands for a woman or girl.

clue.text: Don't keep mum's "restraint underwear"

blocks.note: a let is an obstacle, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance
a slip is a petticoat

explanation.surface: Mum's restrictive underwear, a corset or girdle, put in inverted commas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, with her underwear; in 'keep mum' it means silent, and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret accidentally is to fail to stay quiet about it.

clue.text: Republican party welcoming American leader in peace? That's absurd!

definitions.note: the definition is a description: a paradox is something absurd

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
the earlier words are placed in the word for peace, which wraps around them

blocks.note: pax is Latin for peace
the standard abbreviation
the first letter
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The idea of the Republican party bringing peace, scoffed at as absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory statement or situation seems impossible or nonsensical on its face.

clue.text: Sexually transmitted disease one caught in hay, recklessly – result of getting too high?

indicators.note: doing things recklessly means without order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the pox is an old name for syphilis
the Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: Catching an infection from a careless roll in the hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught in' looks like a container signal but it is part of the surface; all the letters are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen deficiency in the body is a danger for climbers and pilots at altitude, where air is thin.

clue.text: Roger not stuffing without kinky gaiters – that's official

indicators.note: without its stuffing, the name keeps only its outside letters
kinky means twisted, so the word after it is twisted into a new order
without in its old sense of outside, so the first part sits around the second

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Roger declines to have sex, put off by kinky gaiters; that's final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, an old sense, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official keeping records, such as of births, marriages and deaths.

clue.text: State rejected sex ring's alfresco area

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for sex is read backwards

blocks.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania
it is a slang word for sex
a ring has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A state shuts down a sex ring operating outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor space next to a house, used for sitting and eating in the open air.

clue.text: Unhealthy as a penis

definitions.note: an adjective meaning like a dick

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for weak or unsound
second meaning: read jokingly as dick plus -y, penis-like

explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British informal for unsound or in poor health, as in a dicky ticker.
explanation.definitionFit: The British colloquial adjective describes a weak organ or shaky condition, and its form jokingly suggests a slang term for the male member.

clue.text: Diabolical day Donald Trump starts salary 'enhancement'

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letters of the two names
an enhancement is a reworking, so the letters before it are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
the initials of the two names
taken as written

explanation.surface: The day the president starts getting a pay rise, sneered at as wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A villainous or wickedly cruel act is fiendish, the work of a devil.

clue.text: Decides sin absolved is not welcomed by Putin?

definitions.note: the definition describes the noun: what Putin does not welcome

indicators.note: absolved means loosed or set free, so these letters are freed from their order

blocks.note: the ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge pronounces a sin forgiven, and asks whether Putin would like that.
explanation.definitionFit: Political opposition and protest against a regime is something the Kremlin famously suppresses.

clue.text: Right into shag (name unknown), screamer uses it to full effect

definitions.text: screamer uses it to full effect

indicators.note: the first word is put into the slang word, which wraps around it

blocks.note: lay is slang for sex
the standard abbreviation
the standard abbreviation
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A wild night with a stranger, and someone screaming in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Shag is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat produces sound, so anyone shrieking loudly is working it hard.

clue.text: Any more sad, May-made-stateless land workers?

indicators.note: sad in the sense of sorry or in a bad way, so the two words are broken up and rearranged
made stateless means stripped of a state abbreviation, so those letters are cut from the name

blocks.note: taken as written
Theresa May, then Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Farm workers left without a nation by Theresa May's Brexit policy, asking sadly whether there will be any more.
explanation.walkthrough: MA is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, so May without it leaves Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were farmers working their own small holdings, so the collective term covers that class of cultivators.

clue.text: Pence gutted – replaced by greens, if you like!

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters of the name
the lost insides are replaced, so the next word goes into the gap

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
leas are meadows, green fields

explanation.surface: Mike Pence is ousted and replaced by the Green Party, if you fancy that.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Pence was Trump's vice-president; greens suggests the political party but means grassy fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a polite request, the word adds courtesy just as 'if you would' does.

clue.text: Feature of Washington: obnoxious Trump's overbearing manner starts to be restrained by political support group

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of each of the four preceding words
something restrained is held in, so the initials go inside the group

blocks.note: a political action committee, the US fundraising body
the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Trump's overbearing ways being reined in by a lobby group in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac river flows past the US capital and is one of its best-known landmarks.

clue.text: Lengthen pecker? Much of it involves hassle

indicators.note: much of it means a large part of the phrase, a run of letters lying inside it

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: An advert-style offer to enlarge a man's member, and a sly question about whether it's worth the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Pecker is slang for penis, and keep your pecker up is a British phrase for staying cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag and bully a partner, typically a husband, persistently is to harass them.

clue.text: Aggressive sex, perverse sex, in dump

indicators.note: the earlier words sit in the word for a dump, which wraps around them

blocks.note: a hole is a squalid place, a dump
a sexually transmitted infection, the risk of perverse sex

explanation.surface: Rough, kinky sex in a squalid hovel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone combative and unfriendly is antagonistic and ready to attack.

clue.text: Mixer produced by former non-drinker astride a dog?

indicators.note: a rider astride something has legs on either side, so the first part straddles the second

blocks.note: ex means former
TT means teetotal
Rover is a classic dog's name

explanation.surface: A cocktail mixer made by an ex-teetotaller sitting on a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixer' suggests a drink to go with the non-drinker, but it means a sociable person.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person who mingles easily at parties is a good socialiser.

clue.text: What's left of New Hampshire, say

blocks.note: an example of an E(astern) state of the USA, split as E and STATE

explanation.surface: A wry question about what remains of New Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: New Hampshire is a state in the east of the USA, so it is an E state; E is the usual abbreviation for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the property and money they bequeath at death.

clue.text: Horny thing's ready

definitions.note: the slang noun, as in the ready, cash

blocks.note: first meaning: an animal with a horn on its nose
second meaning: old British slang for money, the ready

explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny thing's ready' reads as a sexual come-on. Rhino and the ready are both old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is famous for its nasal horn, and in dated British slang the word also means money, like readies.

clue.text: Brenda's standing with faction 'Remain'

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means read from the bottom upward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER
a side is a faction in a dispute

explanation.surface: The Queen's stance, siding with the Remain campaign in the Brexit vote.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth II Brenda; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on or live somewhere is to dwell there, keeping one's place.

clue.text: Region of mediocrity decentralised America

indicators.note: with its centre taken away, the abbreviation loses its middle letter

blocks.note: pap is bland, worthless stuff
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A comment on a dull, power-devolved America.
explanation.definitionFit: Papua is the territory forming the southern part of New Guinea, now in Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: see 6dn.
Having got firm, corporation on e-trail

definitions.note: a participial phrase standing for the adjective swollen and rigid

blocks.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly
e as written plus scent, a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A company that has become stable thanks to its online presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having got firm' reads as a business establishing itself, and corporation as a company; both are sexual and bodily jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something swollen and stiffened, as tissue becomes when engorged.

clue.text: Conservative leader's rip-off 'buried' in the last month – blame her!

definitions.note: the definition is the person to blame

indicators.note: the leader of the party word is its opening letter
off means wrong or awry, so the three letters are put out of order
something buried lies inside, so the jumbled letters go into the abbreviation for last month

blocks.note: the first letter
ult, short for ultimo, means in last month in old business letters
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader's swindle hushed up last month, with the blame pinned on her.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Theresa May, Tory leader at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilty party responsible for a wrong is the person deserving the fault.

clue.text: Will's appendage bones looped over, having chip on one length

indicators.note: looped over means turned back on itself, so the nickname runs backwards

blocks.note: Bones is Dr McCoy's nickname in Star Trek, so a doc
IC is an integrated circuit, a silicon chip
the Roman numeral
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone called Will has an extra limb, bones twisted and a chip on his shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: Will looks like a man's name; it is a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement added to a testament to amend or extend it is attached to that document.
